### **ASSISTANT** — 2026-07-17 09:05 UTC

I think this is the most important document we'll write for LoreCanvas.

If someone asked me **"What makes LoreCanvas different from Obsidian, Notion, Campfire, or World Anvil?"**, my answer would be:

> **The Node Model.**

Everything else grows from this.

So let's finish it properly.

---

# LTS-003
# Node Specification (Final)

---

# Node Philosophy

A Node represents **one conceptual entity** within a Project.

It is **not**:

- a page
- a document
- a note
- a text file

A Node is an identity.

Examples:

```
Character

Location

Organization

Kingdom

Item

Creature

Magic System

Religion

Language

Vehicle

Historical Event

Planet
```

Cards describe the Node.

Links connect Nodes.

Queries discover Nodes.

Templates create Nodes.

The Node itself simply **exists**.

---

# Purpose

The Node Engine is responsible for representing the identity of every worldbuilding object.

Every meaningful thing inside LoreCanvas is represented by exactly one Node.

---

# Core Responsibilities

The Node Engine owns:

- Identity
- Type
- Status
- Metadata
- Card References
- Link References
- Registration
- Validation
- Lifecycle

Nothing else.

---

# Non-Responsibilities

Nodes never:

Store biographies

Store descriptions

Store notes

Store images

Store histories

Store relationship logic

Store query logic

Save themselves

Render UI

All of those belong elsewhere.

---

# Identity Model

Every Node contains:

```
Node ID

UUID v7

Immutable
```

```
Display Name

Editable
```

```
Type

Immutable
```

```
Status

Mutable
```

```
Project ID

Immutable
```

```
Creation Timestamp

Immutable
```

```
Modified Timestamp

Automatic
```

The Node's identity never changes.

Its metadata may.

---

# Node Invariants

The following must **always** be true:

A Node belongs to exactly one Project.

A Node has exactly one immutable ID.

A Node has exactly one immutable Type.

A Node may have zero Cards.

A Node may have zero Links.

A Node must always exist inside the Repository.

A Node cannot exist outside a Project.

Cards cannot exist without a Node.

Deleting a Node never silently destroys dependent data.

These are architectural guarantees.

Every engine may safely assume they are always true.

---

# Node Types

Built-in types:

Character

Location

Organization

Species

Item

Creature

Event

Timeline Entry

Magic System

Religion

Language

Faction

Government

Culture

Technology

Vehicle

Planet

Dimension

Custom Type

Future versions may add more.

Existing projects remain compatible.

---

# Node Metadata

Metadata describes the Node itself.

Never the story.

Supported metadata:

Display Name

Alias List

Color

Icon

Tags

Creation Date

Modified Date

Archive Date

Author

Visibility

Status

Custom Metadata

Metadata should remain lightweight.

---

# Status Model

Every Node exists in one state.

```
Draft

↓

Active

↓

Archived

↓

Deleted
```

Only valid transitions are allowed.

---

# Lifecycle

Every Node follows:

```
Create

↓

Validate

↓

Register

↓

Available

↓

Modify Metadata

↓

Archive

↓

Restore

↓

Soft Delete

↓

Permanent Delete
```

Skipping lifecycle stages is prohibited.

---

# Registration

Creating a Node does not make it available.

Only the Repository registers Nodes.

Example:

```
Create Node

↓

Repository Validation

↓

Repository Registration

↓

Available
```

This ensures uniqueness and consistency.

---

# Ownership Rules

Nodes own:

Identity

Metadata

Card References

Link References

Nodes do not own:

Card Content

Link Logic

Queries

Templates

Workspace State

Persistence

---

# Relationships

Every Node may reference:

Zero or more Cards

Zero or more Links

Nodes never directly contain another Node.

Relationships always occur through Links.

---

# Validation Rules

Before registration:

Required:

Unique ID

Display Name

Node Type

Project ID

Forbidden:

Duplicate IDs

Null Type

Missing Project

Invalid Status

Repository bypass

---

# Rename Rules

Renaming changes:

Display Name

Only.

Everything else remains identical.

References never break.

---

# Type Rules

Node Type is immutable.

Example:

```
Character

≠

Kingdom
```

Changing type requires creating a new Node.

This prevents hidden data corruption.

---

# Card Rules

Cards always belong to one Node.

Nodes may contain:

Zero

One

Many

Cards.

No limit is imposed by the Node Engine.

---

# Link Rules

Nodes never know how Links work.

They only reference them.

The Link Engine owns relationship behavior.

---

# Search Identity

Queries search Nodes.

Not Cards.

Cards contribute searchable content, but the search result is always the Node that owns them.

This keeps search behavior predictable.

---

# Import Rules

Imported Nodes keep:

UUID (if no conflict exists)

Creation Date

Metadata

Cards

Links

If an ID conflict occurs, conflict resolution is handled by the Repository, not the Node Engine.

---

# Export Rules

Nodes export only:

Identity

Metadata

References

Cards and Links are exported through their own engines to preserve separation of responsibilities.

---

# Performance Expectations

Node metadata should load quickly.

Card content should be loaded lazily.

Large projects should display Node lists without loading every Card.

Node lookup by ID should be constant-time where practical through indexing.

---

# Error Handling

Errors should be explicit.

Good example:

```
Cannot register Node.

Reason:
Duplicate UUID.

Suggested action:
Generate a new ID or resolve the conflict.
```

Avoid vague messages such as "Operation failed."

---

# Security Principles

Nodes never execute code.

Nodes never contain scripts.

Nodes never perform file operations.

Only the Repository coordinates persistence.

---

# Worked Examples

### Example 1: Empty Character

```
Character

Name:
Arin

Cards:
None

Links:
None
```

This is a perfectly valid Node.

---

### Example 2: Developed Character

```
Character

↓

Biography Card

Appearance Card

Personality Card

Inventory Card

Relationship Card
```

The Character remains one Node.

---

### Example 3: Kingdom

```
Kingdom

↓

History Card

Government Card

Economy Card

Military Card
```

Again, one identity with multiple pieces of information.

---

# Acceptance Criteria

The Node Specification is complete when:

- Every Node has a clear identity.
- Ownership boundaries are unambiguous.
- Lifecycle is fully defined.
- Validation rules are complete.
- Import/export behavior is documented.
- Search behavior is defined.
- Performance expectations are established.
- Examples demonstrate correct usage.

---

# Open Questions

These may be revisited without changing the architecture:

- Should aliases participate in search ranking?
- Should Node icons come from a built-in library or user assets?
- Should custom metadata support validation schemas?

---

# Implementation Notes

- IDs should use UUID v7 (or another time-sortable unique identifier).
- Repository remains the only engine that can register or remove Nodes.
- Nodes should expose only public interfaces.
- Card loading should remain lazy to keep large projects responsive.
- Future features such as cloud sync or collaboration must preserve Node identity and invariants.

---

# **LTS-003 Status: COMPLETE** ✅

## Progress Check

We now have:

- ✅ LTS-000 Project
- ✅ LTS-001 Core Standards
- ✅ LTS-003 Node

At this point, I think the **foundation of LoreCanvas is effectively complete**. Everything else, Cards, Links, Queries, Templates, Repository, Storage, Workspace, and Plugins, now builds on a stable definition of what the application's core object actually is.

From here, **LTS-004: Card Specification** will become much easier because we've already answered the most important question: *what a Card belongs to and what it is allowed to do*. That lets us focus entirely on how knowledge is represented, without redefining identity. I expect the Card specification to be the second-largest document in the LTS because it will define the entire knowledge model of LoreCanvas.
